notes: L in all effect text refers to the current Level of this skill.
Rank 2 typically follows the pattern: pool expansion + passive regen for the governing stat pool.
governing_stat: the stat whose rank caps this skill's rank.
Setting partitions: mundane (ancient–medieval), industrial (early modern–steam age), future (modern–sci-fi), fantasy (magic/mythological).
requirements type options: stat_min | skill_min | trait | equipment | affinity | style | proficiency

name_of_style.name: name_of_style
name_of_style.subtitle: One-line description of the style
name_of_style.description: Historical/cultural origin and what makes this style mechanically unique. This is the only place for flavor.

requirements.type: stat_min | skill_min | trait | equipment | affinity | style | proficiency

1.effect: Basic attack or active ability.

2.effect: Pool expansion + regen bonus, or strong passive.

3.effect: Power attack, AOE, or utility skill.

4.effect: Passive augment or synergy bonus.

5.effect: Signature ultimate defining the style's identity.

pankration.name: Pankration
pankration.subtitle: Ancient Greek No-Holds-Barred Wrestling
pankration.description: The first recorded Olympic combat sport, combining boxing and wrestling with almost no restrictions. Practiced throughout ancient Greece and the Mediterranean world, it trained warriors to fight on their feet and on the ground using strikes, chokes, joint locks, and throws.

1.name: Clinch Strike
1.effect: Grapple a target and immediately strike for L damage. The grapple check and attack happen simultaneously.

2.name: Iron Conditioning
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to BDY saves vs knockdown and Prone.

3.name: Stranglehold
3.effect: Apply a choke on a Grappled target: they are Immobilized and take L damage per round until they escape (BDY DC L+2).

4.name: Ground Mastery
4.effect: While Grappling, your target loses 1 AP per round. Gain +L to all attacks against Grappled targets.

5.name: Pankratiast's Fury
5.effect: Strike up to L targets in melee range; each hit applies Bleeding and Weakened. Grappled targets take double damage.

kenjutsu.name: Kenjutsu
kenjutsu.subtitle: Classical Japanese Sword Art
kenjutsu.description: The umbrella term for Japanese swordsmanship schools (ryū) that preceded modern kendo. Focuses on practical technique: drawing, cutting, footwork, and situational awareness. Traditions like Tenshin Shōden Katori Shintō-ryū shaped samurai warfare for centuries.

requirements.description: One-handed or two-handed slashing weapon (no ranged weapons)

1.name: Precision Cut
1.effect: +L to hit on Slash attacks. May reroll one damage die and keep the higher result.

2.name: Focused Blade
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L Dodge when you have not attacked yet this turn.

3.name: Iaijutsu Draw
3.effect: If your weapon was sheathed at the start of your turn, draw and strike for 3L damage before the target can react (no Dodge or Block allowed).

4.name: Read the Blade
4.effect: After a successful hit, predict the target's next action type. Gain +L Dodge vs that predicted action until your next turn.

5.name: Perfect Form
5.effect: A flawless cut that cannot be Blocked or Dodged; deal 3L damage and apply Bleeding.

naginata_jutsu.name: Naginata-jutsu
naginata_jutsu.subtitle: Japanese Polearm Tradition
naginata_jutsu.description: The art of the naginata (a bladed polearm), practiced by Buddhist warrior monks (sōhei) and samurai women defending the home. Emphasizes reach control, sweeping strikes, and zone maintenance to hold off multiple opponents.

1.name: Sweeping Strike
1.effect: +L to Slash and Bash attacks. If two or more enemies are adjacent, the strike hits all of them.

2.name: Defensive Reach
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L Block while wielding a reach weapon.

3.name: Spiral Thrust
3.effect: Pierce in a line up to 3 tiles; deal 2L damage to all targets hit and apply Staggered.

4.name: Zone of Steel
4.effect: Enemies entering your reach zone trigger a free Reaction attack at no AP cost.

5.name: Circle of Heaven
5.effect: Spin attack hitting all adjacent and reach-range enemies; deal 2L damage each. Targets hit by two arcs are knocked Prone.

escrima.name: Escrima
escrima.subtitle: Filipino Stick and Blade Fighting (Arnis/Kali)
escrima.description: The national martial art of the Philippines. A weapons-first system built around sticks, bladed weapons, and empty hands, emphasizing fluid transitions between armed and unarmed combat. Historically used by Filipino warriors against Spanish colonizers.

requirements.description: Light melee weapon or unarmed; may use both simultaneously

1.name: Flow Strike
1.effect: +L to hit. On any hit, switch grip or stance for free (armed to unarmed or vice versa).

2.name: Steel Rhythm
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L to attacks when you struck this target last turn.

3.name: Defang the Snake
3.effect: Strike the target's weapon arm: deal L damage and force a BDY save or they drop their weapon and lose 1 AP.

4.name: Pressure Chain
4.effect: After each hit on the same target this turn, gain +1 to the next attack roll (up to +L maximum).

5.name: Maestro's Flow
5.effect: Strike up to 3 times against one or more targets; each hit reduces that target's Dodge by L for the rest of combat.

muay_thai.name: Muay Thai
muay_thai.subtitle: Thai Eight-Limb Kickboxing
muay_thai.description: The national combat sport of Thailand, developed over centuries from the battlefield art of Muay Boran. Uses fists, elbows, knees, and kicks — the eight weapons — along with clinch techniques. Renowned for conditioning, raw power, and relentless forward pressure.

1.name: Eight Limbs
1.effect: +L to unarmed attacks. Each hit has a 1-in-6 chance to apply Stagger.

2.name: Iron Clinch
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to Grapple and clinch checks.

3.name: Knee Burst
3.effect: Clinch and deliver a knee strike: 3L damage that ignores armor DR. Target is Staggered on hit.

4.name: Teep Wall
4.effect: As a Reaction, push kick an approaching enemy back 1 tile and cancel their advance.

5.name: Muay Mat Rush
5.effect: Deliver 3 consecutive unarmed strikes against one target for 3 AP total; each hit applies a random status (Stagger, Bleeding, or Weakened).

roman_legionary.name: Roman Legionary
roman_legionary.subtitle: Roman Close-Formation Warfare
roman_legionary.description: The fighting system of the Roman legions, combining gladius technique, large rectangular scutum use, and close-formation tactics. Drilled for unit cohesion, the legionary fought as part of a line rather than as an individual, using the shield offensively as well as defensively.

requirements.description: Shield equipped and one-handed melee weapon

1.name: Scutum Wall
1.effect: +L Block. When adjacent to at least one shielded ally, also gain +L to attacks.

2.name: Soldier's Will
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to saves vs Fear and Morale effects.

3.name: Testudo Push
3.effect: Shield-bash all enemies directly ahead; push each 1 tile and deal L damage. Enemies who hit an obstacle are knocked Prone.

4.name: Close Order
4.effect: When adjacent to 2 or more shielded allies, melee attacks against you have disadvantage.

5.name: Legionary's Advance
5.effect: Move up to 3 tiles; all adjacent shielded allies may move the same distance at no AP cost. Enemies in your path take L damage.

mongolian_archery.name: Mongolian Archery
mongolian_archery.subtitle: Steppe Composite Bow Tradition
mongolian_archery.description: The mounted archery tradition of the Mongol steppe warriors, using short recurve composite bows designed for use at full gallop. Mongol horse archers could fire accurately while riding in any direction — including directly behind them (the Parthian shot) — making them virtually uncatchable in open terrain.

1.name: Parthian Shot
1.effect: +L to hit when mounted or when you moved this turn. No accuracy penalty for moving before attacking.

2.name: Draw Discipline
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. Ranged attacks cost -1 AP (minimum 1).

3.name: Rain of Arrows
3.effect: Loose a volley into a 3-tile radius zone; all targets take L damage and are Slowed until their next turn.

4.name: Cavalry Precision
4.effect: While mounted, ranged attacks deal +L damage and ignore half cover bonuses.

5.name: Steppe Ghost
5.effect: Loose two arrows at any targets within range; if the first arrow hits, the second costs 0 AP.

bartitsu.name: Bartitsu
bartitsu.subtitle: Edwardian Eclectic Self-Defense System
bartitsu.description: Developed in London in 1899 by Edward Barton-Wright, the world's first deliberately synthesized martial art. Combines English boxing, French savate footwork, Swiss wrestling, and Japanese jujutsu. Designed for educated gentlemen who might face street violence, it emphasizes improvised weapons, redirection, and tactical awareness over raw strength.

requirements.description: Walking stick, cane, or umbrella (or unarmed)

1.name: Gentleman's Guard
1.effect: +L Dodge. When armed with a cane, parry melee attacks for +L Block as a free Reaction once per round.

2.name: Scientific Approach
2.effect: Max MP +4L. Gain L² MP regen per round. Once per turn, one attack or defensive action costs -1 AP.

3.name: Redirect and Throw
3.effect: Disarm a melee attacker and throw them: target drops their weapon, is knocked Prone, and takes L damage.

4.name: Studied Opponent
4.effect: After observing an enemy attack twice, predict their strike type. Gain +L defense vs that attack type for the rest of combat.

5.name: Grand Synthesis
5.effect: Make a combined attack and counter simultaneously: deal 2L damage and counter-throw for L additional damage. Both effects apply even if the initial attack is blocked.

savate.name: Savate
savate.subtitle: French Scientific Kickboxing
savate.description: Developed in early 19th century France, savate (boxe française) treats the foot as a precision weapon. Unlike most kicking arts, savate practitioners traditionally fought in shoes, allowing harder impacts. Sailors and street fighters in Marseille and Paris developed the style before it was refined into a competitive sport.

1.name: Chassé
1.effect: +L to kick attacks. Kicks deal one damage tier higher than unarmed punches.

2.name: French Footwork
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L Dodge when you moved before attacking this turn.

3.name: Fouetté Tournant
3.effect: Spinning heel kick: deal 3L damage and apply Stagger. If target is already Staggered, knock them Prone instead.

4.name: Measure Control
4.effect: Kicks made against targets entering your zone deal +L damage and deny their melee attack that action.

5.name: Coup de Grâce
5.effect: A precision kick to a vital point: deal 3L damage ignoring half DR. Targets below 25% HP are automatically Staggered.

naval_cutlass.name: Naval Cutlass
naval_cutlass.subtitle: Age of Sail Boarding Combat
naval_cutlass.description: The fighting art of naval boarding actions during the Age of Sail (17th–19th century). Sailors and marines trained with the cutlass for close-quarters combat in the confined, unstable environment of a ship deck. Emphasizes aggressive forward pressure, short powerful cuts, and off-hand use for balance and pistol work.

requirements.description: One-handed slashing weapon; light or medium armor

1.name: Boarding Rush
1.effect: +L to hit when charging. Charge distance is extended by 1 tile.

2.name: Salt Air Grit
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to saves vs environmental hazards (falling, difficult terrain, weather).

3.name: Press Gang Shove
3.effect: Powerful bull-rush: deal 2L damage and shove target up to 2 tiles. Target falls Prone if they collide with an obstacle.

4.name: Reckless Cut
4.effect: May sacrifice defense for offense: gain +L damage on all attacks, but attacks against you have +L to hit until your next turn.

5.name: No Quarter
5.effect: When any adjacent enemy drops below L HP, gain a free bonus attack against them at no additional AP cost.

classical_boxing.name: Classical Boxing
classical_boxing.subtitle: Marquess of Queensberry Rules
classical_boxing.description: The gentleman's sport of the Victorian industrial era, codified by the Marquess of Queensberry rules in 1867. Built around padded gloves, rounds, and prohibitions on wrestling, classical boxing emphasizes footwork, punch accuracy, and guard management as a complete self-defense system.

1.name: Jab
1.effect: +L to unarmed attacks. Once per round, the first unarmed attack costs 1 AP instead of 2.

2.name: Guard Up
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L Block vs unarmed and light weapon attacks.

3.name: Cross-Hook Combo
3.effect: A two-punch combination: the cross lowers target defense by L, and the following hook deals 3L damage.

4.name: Slip and Step
4.effect: Once per round, step out of melee range without provoking Reaction attacks after making an attack.

5.name: Knockout Artist
5.effect: When target is Staggered, the next punch is an automatic critical hit and applies Prone.

bayonet_fighting.name: Bayonet Fighting
bayonet_fighting.subtitle: Military Rifle and Blade Drill
bayonet_fighting.description: The regulated system of bayonet drill taught to infantry from the 18th through early 20th centuries. A practical system for when firearms are empty or close combat is unavoidable, combining thrusting, clubbing with the rifle butt, and footwork from fencing. Used extensively from the Napoleonic Wars through World War I.

requirements.description: Two-handed piercing weapon or rifle with bayonet (spear, pike, or equivalent)

1.name: Fixed Bayonet
1.effect: +L to Stab attacks. Charge attacks deal +L bonus damage.

2.name: Soldier's Endurance
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to saves vs fatigue and forced march penalties.

3.name: Butt Strike
3.effect: Bash with the weapon's butt end: deal 2L damage and apply Stagger. This attack ignores shields.

4.name: Hold the Line
4.effect: While stationary, opportunity attacks against approaching enemies gain +L damage.

5.name: Sergeant's Form
5.effect: Stab and immediately follow with a butt strike as one action. If both hit, the target is knocked Prone.

la_canne.name: La Canne
la_canne.subtitle: French Athletic Cane Fighting
la_canne.description: A French martial art developed in the 19th century that treats the walking cane as a sporting weapon, emphasizing speed, agility, and economy of motion. Developed in the same Paris sporting culture as savate, la canne de combat remains a competitive art today with its distinctive upright guard and angled striking patterns.

requirements.description: Staff, cane, club, or light bludgeoning weapon

1.name: Cane Guard
1.effect: +L to both attack rolls and Dodge. The weapon counts as both offensive and defensive simultaneously.

2.name: Athletic Flow
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L to acrobatic movement and balance checks.

3.name: Redoublement
3.effect: Two rapid strikes at different target locations: each deals L damage. If both hit, apply Stagger.

4.name: Bind and Break
4.effect: On a successful Block, immediately attempt to disarm the attacker as a free Reaction. On success, attacker drops their weapon and is Staggered.

5.name: Passé Supérieur
5.effect: Move through an enemy's space in one fluid step, striking from behind. Target cannot Dodge. Deal 3L damage and apply Bleeding.

krav_maga.name: Krav Maga
krav_maga.subtitle: Israeli Military Self-Defense System
krav_maga.description: Developed by Imi Lichtenfeld for the Israeli Defense Forces, Krav Maga ('contact combat' in Hebrew) is a threat-neutralization system built for real-world violence rather than sport. Draws from boxing, wrestling, judo, and aikido, stripped to the most efficient techniques. Core philosophy: finish the fight as quickly and decisively as possible.

1.name: Threat Neutralize
1.effect: The first attack each combat deals +L damage and cannot be Blocked. Ignore the first Stagger applied to yourself per combat.

2.name: Combat Conditioning
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to saves vs pain-based status effects (Stagger, Weakened).

3.name: Aggressive Counter
3.effect: On any successful Block or Dodge, immediately counter-strike for L damage at 0 additional AP cost.

4.name: Weapon Strip
4.effect: Attempt to disarm an enemy as a 1 AP action. On success, take their weapon and may use it this turn.

5.name: Kill Switch
5.effect: A rapid sequence of disabling strikes: apply Stagger and Immobilized simultaneously. Target cannot use Reactions until end of their next turn.

combat_sambo.name: Combat Sambo
combat_sambo.subtitle: Soviet Military Grappling-Striking Hybrid
combat_sambo.description: Sambo (SAMozashchita Bez Oruzhiya — self-defense without weapons) was developed by the Soviet Red Army in the 1920s, drawing from judo, wrestling, and Slavic fighting traditions. Combat Sambo retains strikes, headbutts, and weapons defense. It is the foundation of Russian special forces training and the backbone of many modern MMA competitors.

1.name: Throw Entry
1.effect: +L to Grapple checks. After any successful Dodge, immediately attempt a free Grapple or throw.

2.name: Wrestler's Build
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. +L to BDY saves vs knockdown and Prone.

3.name: Slam Down
3.effect: Lift and body-slam the target: deal 3L damage and apply Prone and Staggered simultaneously.

4.name: Arm Lock
4.effect: While Grappling, lock a limb: target loses 1 AP per round and cannot use two-handed attacks until the Grapple is broken.

5.name: Ground and Pound
5.effect: While target is Prone or Grappled, deal L damage per AP spent in strikes, up to 3 hits. Each hit costs 1 AP.

brazilian_jiu_jitsu.name: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
brazilian_jiu_jitsu.subtitle: Ground Grappling and Submission Art
brazilian_jiu_jitsu.description: Developed by the Gracie family in Brazil from Mitsuyo Maeda's judo. BJJ proved that ground-fighting and submission holds could neutralize larger, stronger opponents. Practitioners are trained to be comfortable — even dominant — in the most unfavorable positions on the ground.

1.name: Guard Pull
1.effect: +L to Grapple checks. May enter a defensive Grapple (guard) that prevents the enemy from attacking others while you hold them.

2.name: Mat Sense
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. While Prone or Grappled, gain +L to all defensive rolls.

3.name: Submission Lock
3.effect: Lock a joint or apply a choke: target is Immobilized and takes L damage per round until they escape (BDY save DC L+3).

4.name: Inversion Guard
4.effect: While Prone or Grappled, attacks against you cost the attacker +1 AP. Enemies must spend 2 AP to disengage from your guard.

5.name: Tap or Snap
5.effect: Increase Submission Lock damage to 2L per round. Escape requires 4 AP. On a critical fail to escape, target gains Weakened for the rest of combat.

tactical_cqc.name: Tactical CQC
tactical_cqc.subtitle: Modern Military Close Quarters Combat
tactical_cqc.description: Close Quarters Combat doctrine as taught to modern special operations forces worldwide. Integrates firearms, blade, and empty-hand techniques with threat assessment and immediate action in confined spaces such as buildings, vehicles, and ships. Associated with units like Delta Force, SAS, and GSG-9.

1.name: Target Acquisition
1.effect: +L to hit at close range (within 10 ft). No accuracy penalty for switching targets in the same turn.

2.name: Situational Awareness
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L to Perception checks during combat; cannot be Surprised.

3.name: Dynamic Entry
3.effect: Move up to 3 tiles and attack every target in your path; deal L damage to each. Movement does not provoke Reactions.

4.name: Cover to Cover
4.effect: Dash between two pieces of cover using 1 AP; gain +L Dodge until your next turn.

5.name: Lethal Efficiency
5.effect: Whenever you reduce a target to 0 HP this turn, all remaining attack AP costs are reduced by 1 for the rest of that turn.

mixed_martial_arts.name: Mixed Martial Arts
mixed_martial_arts.subtitle: Modern Multi-Discipline Combat Sport
mixed_martial_arts.description: Formalized through the UFC and refined across thousands of professional bouts, modern MMA converges on wrestling for takedowns, BJJ for ground-fighting, and Muay Thai or boxing for striking. Top-level practitioners are complete fighters able to dominate at any range or position.

1.name: Complete Fighter
1.effect: +L to both unarmed strikes and Grapple checks. No penalty for switching between striking and grappling in the same turn.

2.name: Fight Conditioning
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. Reduce duration of Stagger and Weakened applied to you by 1 round (minimum 1).

3.name: Takedown or KO
3.effect: Choose: Takedown (2L damage + Prone + Grapple) or Overhand (2L damage + Stagger). Both options cost the same AP.

4.name: Damage Adaptation
4.effect: After being hit, gain +1 to all defenses until end of your next turn (cumulative, up to +L maximum).

5.name: Full Fight Mode
5.effect: Activate for 3 rounds: gain +L to all attacks, defenses, and damage. Cannot be Staggered while active.

systema.name: Systema
systema.subtitle: Russian Intelligence Body Movement Art
systema.description: A Russian martial art associated with Spetsnaz, developed from Cossack warrior traditions and systematized in the Soviet era. Unlike sport martial arts, systema focuses on natural body movement, breath control under stress, and adaptive principles rather than fixed techniques — making it highly effective against any style or weapon.

1.name: Natural Movement
1.effect: +L Dodge. Moving toward an enemy does not provoke Reaction attacks.

2.name: Breathing Mastery
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. At the start of each turn, remove one Stagger applied to yourself.

3.name: Redirection
3.effect: As a Reaction to a melee attack, redirect it into an adjacent target: the attacker's strike hits a target of your choice adjacent to you.

4.name: Flow State
4.effect: After 3 consecutive successful Dodges or Blocks, gain +L to attacks and +L damage until you take damage.

5.name: Formless
5.effect: For 1 round, become immune to attack types you have already successfully Dodged or Blocked this combat.

war_monk.name: War Monk
war_monk.subtitle: Monastic Temple Guardian Tradition
war_monk.description: The fighting tradition of temple guardians and warrior monks who believe combat is an extension of devotion. Drawing from monastic traditions across cultures — Shaolin, Templar Knights, Yamabushi — war monks train body and spirit together, channeling inner stillness into devastating precision.

requirements.description: Unarmed Attacks or Simple Weapon proficiency
Light or no armor; no heavy weapons

1.name: Disciplined Strike
1.effect: +L to unarmed or simple weapon attacks. Once per turn, add MND rank to damage on one attack.

2.name: Meditative Fortitude
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. While SP is above half, immune to Fear effects.

3.name: Stunning Palm
3.effect: A precise strike to a vital point: deal 2L damage. Target must pass a MND save (DC L+2) or be Stunned for 1 round.

4.name: Step Between Worlds
4.effect: Once per round, teleport 1 tile before or after an attack. Does not provoke Reactions.

5.name: Perfect Stillness
5.effect: For 1 round, become immune to all damage. Any attack that would have hit you is countered for 3L damage.

duellists_code.name: Duellist's Code
duellists_code.subtitle: Classical Fantasy Honor Dueling
duellists_code.description: An ancient tradition of formalized single combat practiced by noble houses, champion warriors, and wandering swordmasters. The duellist's art treats combat as ceremony — a test of perfect technique, composure, and absolute mastery of a single blade. Those who break the Code's unspoken rules of engagement find the tradition itself seems to turn against them.

requirements.description: One-handed melee weapon; no shield; light or medium armor only

1.name: En Garde
1.effect: +L to both attacks and Dodge when fighting a single target. If two or more enemies attack you in one round, this bonus is lost until your next turn.

2.name: Steel Composure
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L to saves vs Intimidation, Fear, and mental effects.

3.name: Fleche
3.effect: A lightning thrust: dash up to 2 tiles and strike for 3L damage. Apply Bleeding on hit.

4.name: Riposte
4.effect: As a Reaction after a successful Dodge, immediately deal L damage to the attacker at no AP cost.

5.name: Final Flourish
5.effect: Declare a formal duel: both you and your named target may only attack each other until one falls. Gain +L to all attack and defense rolls for the duration. If your target flees, they take 2L damage and gain Weakened.

berserker_path.name: Berserker Path
berserker_path.subtitle: Ancient Rage Warrior Tradition
berserker_path.description: The tradition of the berserkr — the Old Norse warrior who fought in a trance-like fury, heedless of wounds, inspired by the bear or wolf spirit they wore. Practiced in saga cultures across the world, the berserker path rejects technique in favor of overwhelming violence and supernatural endurance, fueling power from pain and bloodshed.

requirements.description: Melee weapon; light or no armor preferred

1.name: Battle Fury
1.effect: +L damage when HP is below half. Immune to Morale penalties and Frightened.

2.name: Blood Surge
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. Each time you deal damage, regain 1 HP.

3.name: Reckless Charge
3.effect: Charge up to 4 tiles, dealing 3L damage on impact. You take L damage yourself — this fuels your fury.

4.name: Unyielding
4.effect: Once per round, when damage would reduce you to 0 HP, remain at 1 HP instead and gain +L to all attacks until end of your next turn.

5.name: Ulfhednar's Form
5.effect: Enter a battle trance: gain +2L to all attacks, damage, and BDY saves for 5 rounds. When the trance ends, gain Weakened and Staggered from exhaustion.

shadow_step.name: Shadow Step
shadow_step.subtitle: Phantom Assassin's Tradition
shadow_step.description: The killing art of assassin orders and shadow cults who have learned to use darkness as weapon and shield. Where mundane rogues merely hide in shadows, shadow step practitioners have merged their movement with darkness — slipping between shaded spaces, striking from concealment, and vanishing before the body hits the ground.

requirements.description: Light weapon; light or no armor

1.name: Shade Step
1.effect: +L to attacks from concealment or when unseen. As a 1 AP action, enter Stealth if shadows or dim light are present.

2.name: Veil of Silence
2.effect: Max SP +4L. Gain L² SP regen per round. +L to Stealth checks made during combat.

3.name: Mark and Vanish
3.effect: Strike from concealment for 2L damage, then immediately re-enter Stealth as part of the same action.

4.name: Death from Nowhere
4.effect: Your first attack from Stealth each round is an automatic critical hit and does not break Stealth if the target survives.

5.name: Phantom
5.effect: Merge with shadows for 3 rounds: gain full invisibility. Attacks do not break invisibility unless you miss.

arcane_bladework.name: Arcane Bladework
arcane_bladework.subtitle: Spell-Sword Melee Magic Integration
arcane_bladework.description: The tradition of warrior-mages who refuse to choose between blade and spell. Where most magical traditions demand stillness and focus, arcane bladework trains the practitioner to cast while moving, striking, and taking hits — weaving spells into weapon swings and delivering them on contact. Most mages consider it wasteful. Most warriors consider it showing off.

1.name: Spell-Forged Strikes
1.effect: +L to weapon attacks. Deals +L elemental damage matching your primary affinity on each hit.

2.name: Mana Flow
2.effect: Max MP +4L. Gain L² MP regen per round. Casting spells no longer interrupts melee stance or costs additional AP.

3.name: Runic Slash
3.effect: Charge the blade with spell energy; deliver on next hit for +2L elemental damage plus the status effect associated with your affinity.

4.name: Counter-Weave
4.effect: On a successful Dodge vs a magical or ranged attack, absorb L MP from the spell or projectile.

5.name: Convergence
5.effect: Simultaneously make a weapon attack and cast a Rank 3 or higher spell at the same target. Both resolve at full power as a single action.

divine_guardian.name: Divine Guardian
divine_guardian.subtitle: Sacred Warrior of Faith
divine_guardian.description: The martial tradition of those sworn to a divine power — paladins, templar knights, warrior-priests, and sacred defenders. Divine guardians do not merely fight for their god; they become instruments of divine will in combat. The tradition teaches that the highest expression of faith is an unbroken shield wall between the innocent and the darkness.

requirements.description: Melee weapon and shield or heavy armor

1.name: Sacred Ward
1.effect: +L Block and +L to saves vs undead and demonic effects. Weapon deals +L Radiant damage vs unholy targets.

2.name: Blessed Endurance
2.effect: Max HP +4L. Gain L² HP regen per round. Heal L HP on each successful Block.

3.name: Holy Smite
3.effect: Call divine power into a strike: deal 3L Radiant damage. Undead and Demons take double damage from this attack.

4.name: Lay on Hands
4.effect: Heal an adjacent ally for 2L HP. May be used once per round as a 1 AP action.

5.name: Divine Bulwark
5.effect: Invoke divine protection for 3 rounds: you and all adjacent allies gain +L DR and immunity to Fear.

spellslinger.name: Spellslinger
spellslinger.subtitle: Ranged Affinity Delivery — Bolt Style
spellslinger.description: A caster trained to project any known Affinity as a high-velocity piercing bolt. Spellslingers channel whatever energies they have attuned into fast, accurate ranged strikes. A Fire 1 / Water 1 / Steam 1 Spellslinger can throw any of three bolt types, adapting to the situation. Informally called glass cannons.

1.name: Bolt
1.effect: Cast any known Affinity as a bolt: deal L [piercing] damage at 3L spaces range and apply L stacks of that Affinity status.

2.name: Arcane Reserve
2.effect: Max MP +L². MPR +L.

3.name: Scatter Shot
3.effect: Fire L bolts that may each target a different enemy within 3L spaces: deal L [piercing + Affinity] damage per bolt and apply L stacks of [Affinity Status] to each target hit.

4.name: Penetrating Charge
4.effect: Bolts that hit a target already at maximum [Affinity Status] stacks deal bonus L [Affinity] damage and reset stacks to L.

5.name: Singularity
5.effect: Fire a hyper-condensed bolt of [Affinity] energy: deal 5L [piercing + Affinity] damage. Ignores all resistances. Applies L² stacks of [Affinity Status].

battlemage.name: Battlemage
battlemage.subtitle: Affinity-Infused Melee Style
battlemage.description: Warriors who channel attuned Affinities directly into weapons and strikes, fusing elemental or emotional energy with close-quarters combat.

1.name: Charged Strike
1.effect: Strike with a weapon infused with [Affinity] energy: deal weapon damage + L [Affinity] damage. Apply L stacks of [Affinity Status] on hit.

2.name: Battle Temper
2.effect: Max SP +L². SPR +L. +L to BDY saves vs knockdown while in melee.

3.name: Runic Burst
3.effect: Release stored [Affinity] energy in a devastating strike: deal 3L [Affinity] damage and apply [Affinity Status] to all within L tiles of your target.

4.name: Energy Return
4.effect: Each melee hit that applies [Affinity Status] restores L SP. While your [Affinity] level is at or above this Style level, weapon strikes deal +L [Affinity] damage.

5.name: Runic Annihilation
5.effect: Channel all [Affinity Status] stacks on your target into a catastrophic strike: deal 5L [Affinity] damage. Each stack consumed adds +L bonus damage.

channeler.name: Channeler
channeler.subtitle: Sustained Affinity Aura — Field Control Style
channeler.description: Casters who project Affinity energy as a sustained emanating field rather than targeted strikes. Channelers reshape the battlefield through continuous energy exposure.

1.name: Energy Veil
1.effect: Project [Affinity] energy as a sustained aura centered on yourself for L rounds. Allies within L tiles gain +L to [relevant stat]. Enemies who begin their turn in the aura take L [Affinity] damage.

2.name: Deep Current
2.effect: Max MP +L². MPR +L. Aura abilities cost 1 less MP (min 1) while you have more than half your MP.

3.name: Resonance Field
3.effect: Expand your aura to L×2 tile radius for L rounds. Allies gain +L to all rolls. Enemies in the field lose L [stat] for the duration.

4.name: Attunement Surge
4.effect: Your aura persists at half cost (round up) when you have more than half your MP. Allies starting their turn in your aura may reroll one die on their next roll.

5.name: Avatar Form
5.effect: Fully manifest [Affinity] energy for L rounds: aura covers the entire encounter area. Allies double all aura bonuses. Enemies suffer [Affinity Status] at maximum potency each round.

warden.name: Warden
warden.subtitle: Elemental Barrier — Defensive Casting Style
warden.description: Casters who manifest Affinity energy as barriers and reactive shields. Every attack absorbed becomes an opportunity to retaliate.

1.name: Elemental Guard
1.effect: Raise an [Affinity] barrier: gain +L to Block or Dodge for L rounds. When the barrier absorbs a hit, deal L [Affinity] damage to the attacker as a Reaction.

2.name: Fortified Reserve
2.effect: Max MP +L². MPR +L. +L to saves vs [Affinity] damage.

3.name: Barrier Pulse
3.effect: Release your barrier as a shockwave: deal 2L [Affinity] damage in a L-tile radius and push all hit targets back L tiles. Barrier resets to full strength.

4.name: Passive Shield
4.effect: Your barrier rebuilds at the start of each of your turns (restores L barrier HP, max L²). Attacks against targets you are blocking deal +L [Affinity] damage.

5.name: Absolute Aegis
5.effect: Raise an impenetrable [Affinity] barrier for L rounds. You and adjacent allies cannot take damage from sources you choose. When it expires, it detonates for 3L [Affinity] damage to all enemies in the area.
